description_full: ARYZTA AG provides products and services for in-store bakery solutions in Europe and internationally. It offers pastries, cookies, buns, breads, rolls, artisan loaves, sweet baked goods, morning goods, and savoury and other products. The company is also involved in asset management services; and distribution of food products. In addition, it serves grocery, convenience, and independent retailers, as well as quick service restaurants (QSR) and other foodservice customers under the Hiestand, Mette Munk, Pre Pain, Cuisine de France, Coup de Pates, La Carte, Oh My Sweetness, and Fornetti brands. ARYZTA AG was incorporated in 2023 and is headquartered in Schlieren, Switzerland.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 7K people. Revenue per employee of $319K ranks in the below the sector median among Consumer Defensive peers. Each employee generates $23K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $315 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: ARYZTA AG is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.3B market cap on $2.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 12% against a 8% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $178M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.5×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.9% of the shares.

sect: Its 8% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Defensive median (7%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.97x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.07 across 172 companies in the universe; the top four hold 38% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 20% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 2928% and a beta of 1.00, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -11.94 vs 5y -1.17), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $6K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 91% in the 2020 crash and 19% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 47% below its DCF fair value of $94.37, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 14%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $71.68 to $128 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Defensive peers: P/E 10.2 vs 18.5 and P/FCF 7.0 vs 16.0 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 14.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 7.9% annual cash-flow growth, 11pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 12% earns above the cost of capital of 8.2%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.42).
It runs a 19% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.29x.
ROE of 20% is amplified by 3.4x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.1x net debt to EBITDA ($76.4M of cash against $796.2M of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 3.5x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.99 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.58 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 8.7% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders own 6.9%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 56%.
people: With about 7,774 employees, each generates about $319K of revenue, 0.6x the Consumer Defensive median.
That works out to $23K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $414K (1x revenue per employee).
